bluf: Brafton is a US content marketing agency selling content, SEO, PPC, email and web work on its own platform, contentmarketing.ai, and it calls itself the world's best content marketing agency of 2026. Its record shows a busy house: 209 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, 69 Google ads, and SEO prices published down to $1 per word. It sells GEO services and ChatGPT Ads yet publishes no llms.txt. The one thing a rival should know: Horus reads it Neutral at 5.6 and most exposed to KJ6, the hollowed out agency middle, and the Monsoon displacement of 67.8 says its book very likely buys on price.
doing:
Brafton positions itself as a content marketing agency powered by its own content platform, pairing marketing data with in house writers, designers and video producers: in plain words, a production shop that staffs its own makers and runs them on its own software. Its headline claim is that it is the world's best content marketing agency of 2026, and its PPC page says Google Premier Partner status puts it in the top 3% of the partner program.

The mix is broad, twelve services from Content Writing Services to ChatGPT Ads. The lead line is Content & Digital PR at 3: the homepage title and H1 lead with content marketing. Five core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO rests on GEO and ChatGPT Ads pages and on case studies counting AI Overview citations for Beca and ManagedMethods. Email & CRM rests on campaign management, a HubSpot Platinum Solutions Partner badge and 700+ emails across four DTC brands for 33 Threads. Paid Search rests on the PPC page as a Google Premier and Microsoft Advertising partner and on cases for On Call International and CFGI. SEO rests on agency and pricing pages, and cases for ManagedMethods, Webex and Rosterfy. Web & Product rests on web design and UX services and builds for Clemens Food Group, Amphenol Alden and Vidcast. Proprietary: contentmarketing.ai and the Search Performance Brief.

Its AI posture is commercial: GEO services and ChatGPT Ads management sold beside SEO content, AI Overview citations reported in case studies, and its own content platform; AI Automation / Agents scores 1 with no evidence note.

The record lists no dated moves, news or jobs. Pricing is public and unit based: audits $600 to $8,000, technical SEO consulting $200 per hour, keyword briefs $300 each, SEO content $1 per word. Absent for a company of its kind: no office listed, ownership unknown, programmatic and retail media at 0.
clients:
The record marks its client type as mixed and lists eight verticals: SaaS and technology; fintech, accounting and credit unions; healthcare, pharma and dental; education and higher ed; legal; manufacturing; recruiting; ecommerce. The home market is the US; no office is listed.

The book holds 14 clients, 11 with observed needs and 3 names only. Organic demand leads with 5 clients, paid performance 4, brand and creative 2, AI and automation 2, and CRM, commerce, social, web and local lead generation 1 each. Organic names: ManagedMethods (14 blogs turned into page 1 rankings and 200 backlinks), Webex (blog SEO), MIT Sloan (link building that boosted page authority across key URLs), Beca (8 blogs that captured AI driven search visibility, organic plus AI) and TruGreen (SEO and GEO organic growth strategies, organic, local lead generation and AI). Paid names: On Call International and CFGI (PPC services page), Ameritas (PPC campaigns for brand awareness and buy in, paid plus brand) and Gasper (paid social). 33 Threads came for CRM and commerce (scaling email across four DTC brands), Vidcast for brand and web (a new website design around its visual first ethos).

Three are names only, need inferred from the content lead: LeQuest (a portfolio slug on dual white papers for two healthcare audiences), Oxford University Press (a portfolio slug) and Oliver Wight (a testimonial on the about page).

No client on record sits on another tracked agency's book.

KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is its best placed judgment, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the organic names ask for citation share beside rankings next; KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) is its exposure, so per word content hours are, at a roughly even chance, the first line these clients cut.
house: Three say and do tests sit on its house and the record marks 2 of 3 practised. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while its sitemap holds 41 AI topic URLs, the one gap the Radar lists; no AI crawlers are blocked. Paid Search is corroborated by its own Google ads and publishing cadence by 209 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 565 in 365 out of 8043. The tag stack is gtm, ga4, meta_pixel, linkedin_insight, hubspot, ms_clarity, vwo and cookieyes on WordPress: Meta and LinkedIn pixels, VWO for testing, no ABM stack. Its Google Ads Transparency Center record shows 69 ads, 36 text, 18 image and 15 video, 24 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-27; one sample reads "Increase visibility in AI driven search and ChatGPT results". Its LinkedIn record shows 1 company ad and 0 thought leader ads. No Meta or TikTok check is recorded.
market:
The Horus read puts Brafton at a tailwind index of 5.6, band Neutral. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) at net 0.306, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and for KJ2 at 0.175; it is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) at -0.506. The best scenario fit is The Toll Road at 38/100. It is making P7 (owned audience hedges); P1 (audited AI visibility), P4 (inputs for automation) and P8 (ads inside assistants) are partial; P2, P3, P5 and P6 are absent, P5 because it publishes hourly rates.

The Monsoon read is 62.3, band Onshore wind, migration 56.8 against displacement 67.8, observed via the hourly pricing term. 57 of the index is the sold mix, with SEO (9) and Web & Product (9) most movable; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. No hub office is listed, footprint inferred, yet it claims onshore delivery: in house writers, designers and video producers.
openings:
The strongest opening is price. The Monsoon displacement of 67.8 and public unit rates ($200 per hour, $1 per word) make it very likely, with high confidence, that an offshore delivered rival undercuts its SEO content and web hours line by line. The falsifier is its pricing page moving to output or outcome pricing, which would remove the rate a rival prices against.

The contradiction to lead with is AI visibility: it sells GEO and ChatGPT Ads, publishes no llms.txt across 41 AI topic URLs, and P1 is partial with no audited product in the record, so a rival opening with an audited citation number is likely to win the AI conversation with Beca and TruGreen. The related gap is P2: no feed, schema or entity work on its core search and web lines.

Its paid book is contestable on inputs: P4 is partial, with no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth showing, so On Call International, CFGI, Ameritas and Gasper are likely open to a pitch on those inputs. Its in house writers claim against a mix of mostly movable hours is one to test in the sales room.
watch: Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would deepen its KJ6 exposure while it still publishes hourly rates.

Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of its SEO line, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and its ChatGPT Ads bet.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.
Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM would tell whether its ChatGPT Ads line has a market.

Follow up the ad record: Google ads last shown 2026-09-27 with 24 of 69 in the last 30 days against a single LinkedIn company ad, so any LinkedIn build out would signal a B2B pipeline push the record does not yet show.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
